Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for UAE's response with the bat. The umpires make their way out and the Afghans, led by Rashid Khan, spread out from the team huddle to take their positions on the field. Muhammad Waseem walks out to the crease and will be partnered by Muhammad Zohaib. And Afghanistan go with spin straightaway. Mujeeb Ur Rahman to begin the proceedings in the chase. Zohaib to face. Off we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right. 189 it is for the United Arab Emirates to chase and get their first win in this tri-series. But they will need their top order to support senior pros like captain Muhammad Waseem and Asif Khan from the other end. Afghanistan's inning has shown that once you see off the new ball phase with caution, runs can be scored with wickets in hand. However, they will be up against a quality spin trio of Afghanistan on a slowish pitch. It is all set up for an exciting run chase which is on the other side. Stay tuned.

Afghanistan's Sediqullah Atal is up for a quick chat with the broadcasters. Atal says that he is happy with his first T20I fifty but will be happier if they end up on the winning side. Adds that the wicket wasn't as easy as there was some spongy bounce so he took his time. Mentions that after the 5th over, they started counter-attacking and the plan was to put away the loose balls and also run doubles. Ends by saying that they were aiming for something around 160-165, and reckons that this total is enough for them to get over the line.

Again, the death-over phase proved a bit too costly for the UAE bowlers as runs flowed freely in the last stretch. A bit of inexperience was clearly evident. With enough wickets in hand, every incoming batter came out with intent and with the help of late cameos from Karim Janat and Azmatullah Omarzai, Afghanistan managed to smash 62 runs in the last five overs.

The UAE bowlers weren’t poor by any stretch in the first half, yet they will likely feel the rewards didn’t come as often as they deserved. Whether you call it sharp batting or just the way the game unfolded, that’s how it stood. Afghanistan hit a small bump when Haider Ali broke the 84-run second-wicket stand. 100/1 became 120/3, but by then Ibrahim was well set and had brought up his own half-century, setting up for a strong finish. But he couldn't hang in there till the end.

But as soon as the movement faded away, batting appeared to be a bit easier and that's when Sediqullah Atal fueled in some aggression. However, the sluggish nature of the pitch kept the batters in check once the spinners were brought in. However, the partnership took a decent shape between Sediqullah Atal and Ibrahim Zadran. They didn't go bang-bang, but steadied the ship at halfway, adding 31 in the next four after the restrictions lifted. Eventually, Sediqullah got off to his well-constructed fifty, looking to go big.

There was just enough lateral movement early on and UAE’s new ball pair, Junaid Siddique and Muhammad Rohid, made the most of it with disciplined lines. Rahmanullah Gurbaz never looked settled against the swing, and neither did the others sharing the crease. The pacers kept probing in the right areas, inducing a series of false strokes. A few streaky boundaries came off the edge, but the middle of the bat was rarely found. By the end of the Powerplay, Afghanistan were restricted to 43/1 with Gurbaz back in the hut.

Such an anti-climactic end to the innings. A job well done by Junaid Siddique in that final over. He executed four pinpoint yorkers off the six balls, and did not concede a single boundary. He, though, will have to wait for another match to complete 100 T20I wickets. Afghanistan were well within reach to go past 200 runs, but with the last over going for just 5 runs, UAE might feel they have pulled things a bit. However, 188, on a slow Sharjah wicket, is still a huge score to hunt down.

Exceptional last over from Junaid Siddique! Just 5 runs off it! This is a full toss, on off, Azmatullah Omarzai uses his feet and thumps it on the bounce to long off for one more. Afghanistan finishes on 188/4!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. 43/1 in the Powerplay and 31/0 in the next four overs. Afghanistan have slightly snatched the momentum from UAE with alert batting by Sediqullah Atal and Ibrahim Zadran. There is enough for the spinners in the track, but batting has looked far easier against the older ball as compared to the new hard leather. UAE's immediate aim will be to halt this blossoming partnership and induce a collapse, testing the Afghan middle order which looked vulnerable against Pakistan in the series opener. Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness! The two umpires pick up the match ball and make their way out to the middle. United Arab Emirates players follow them and spread out to take their respective field positions. A new opening pair for Afghanistan as ​​​Sediqullah Atal joins Rahmanullah Gurbaz to come out to bat. Junaid Siddique has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Before we start the game, the players from both sides take a moment of silence to pay tribute to the lives lost in last night’s devastating earthquake in Afghanistan, standing in solidarity with all those affected by the tragedy.

UAE's Asif Khan is up for a quick chat with Bazid Khan. He says he has played a lot of domestic cricket in the UAE. Adds that he tries to settle in the first ten balls and then takes the chances and goes aggressive. Mentions this tri-series is a huge opportunity for them to prepare for the upcoming Asia Cup. Details that he just tries to play to his strengths, and also adds that he and Waseem try to contribute as much as they can. Shares that their bowling lineup is very good but admits that they gave away too many runs in the previous game. Highlights that they have done decently against the Test-playing nations in recent times and ends by saying they will take the positives from that to progress ahead.

PITCH REPORT - Aamir Sohail is pitchside for his analysis. He says that there is a bit of moisture on the wicket. Adds that it will initially offer some grip, and the batters need to be patient. Mentions the difference between now and when he played on the surface back in the days is the grass, and that there is no sheen. Ends by saying that it has something for everyone.

The captain of Afghanistan, Rashid Khan, says that they would have batted first and is happy that they got what they wanted to do. On the conversation about playing against different oppositions, Rashid details that they do not see which opposition they are playing against. Says it is all about how they are going to play and that they don't want to repeat the mistakes made in the last game. Informs that they have made one change - Sharafuddin Ashraf comes in for Fareed Ahmad.

The captain of United Arab Emirates, Muhammad Waseem, says that they will bowl first. Adds that no specific reason but the wicket looks good and he hopes that the ball does a bit early on but expect it to not change much in the second innings. Mentions that they have a lot of boundary balls away in the last game and needs to improve on that. Says that they will be happy to restrict Afghanistan under 160. Informs they have made a couple of changes in the side.

United Arab Emirates (Playing XI) - Muhammad Waseem (C), Muhammad Zohaib, Asif Khan, Rahul Chopra (WK), Ethan D'souza, Harshit Kaushik (On T20I debut and in for Alishan Sharafu), Dhruv Parashar, Saghir Khan, Haider Ali, Muhammad Rohid (In for Muhammad Jawadullah), and Junaid Siddique.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Sediqullah Atal, Darwish Rasooli, Karim Janat, Azmatullah Omarzai, Rashid Khan (C), Mohammad Nabi, Sharafuddin Ashraf (In for Fareed Ahmad), Mujeeb Ur Rahman, and Fazalhaq Farooqi.
TOSS UPDATE - The flip of the coin is won by the United Arab Emirates and captain Muhammad Waseem elects to BOWL first.

Two games in Sharjah have told one story clearly. Spin has been the king, pace has been punished. But if a fresh surface is in play this time around, the equation might shift, demanding that both pace units adapt quickly. UAE have two wins in their last six fixtures against Afghanistan, and the most recent coming in December 2023, which is proof that they can land a punch. But the determined Afghan side will be ready to take them head-on. An interesting match-up overall. Toss and teams coming up shortly.

UAE’s homework isn’t any lighter. The top order has to shoulder more responsibility. Leaving the repair work to power-hitter Asif Khan every time isn’t sustainable for the long run. Skipper Muhammad Waseem and the senior batters need support, and they need it early. In the bowling department, the first few overs looked promising, but control evaporated in the middle and death overs. The pacers, led by Muhammad Jawadullah and Junaid Siddique, were scattered across the park. Line, length, and death-ball variations will decide if UAE can contain Afghanistan this time.

For Afghanistan, the task is all about tightening the loose ends. They pushed Pakistan hard, had the game within reach, and still watched it slip badly when the pressure mounted. Their spin core of Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, and Mohammad Nabi delivered exactly what was expected, control and wickets. But the seamers fell short and couldn’t quite match the standards. This is their chance to iron out these wrinkles. With the bat, the top three of Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Ibrahim Zadran, and Darwish Rasooli gave a solid start, but the middle overs became a trap. Too many wickets fell in clusters, momentum drained, and in the end, it cost them the match. Those are the fine margins they’ll be desperate to fix.

Both teams have played once, both have been handed defeats by Pakistan, the current leaders. That’s what makes this one crucial. Win, and you’re still in the race. Lose, and the climb gets steeper. Afghanistan walk in as the favorites, carrying experience and exposure with them. UAE walk in with hunger and a point to prove. Afghanistan will hold their ground in second place, while UAE can climb off the bottom and throw the fight for the final wide open before the reverse fixtures commence.

Sharjah Cricket Ground lights up again after a day’s break as the Tri-Series in the Emirates rolls on. Match 3 is here, and it’s Afghanistan locking horns with the hosts, the United Arab Emirates, in what promises to be a thrilling battle for pride and progress on the international stage. Afghanistan have proven their class at the highest level, while for a young side like the UAE, this is the perfect stage to punch above their weight and shake things up. On that note, hello and welcome, we are excited to have you all with us.

The T20I Tri-Series in UAE, 2025, serves as a crucial prelude to the upcoming Asia Cup, providing Afghanistan, Pakistan, and the United Arab Emirates with an opportunity to fine-tune their strategies and test their squads. The tournament has already seen a couple of matches played, and now the hosts, UAE, are set to face Afghanistan in the third encounter. Both teams will be eager to secure a victory and get their campaign on track. Afghanistan comes into this match having lost their opening game against Pakistan. The team showed flashes of brilliance but struggled to maintain momentum, particularly with the bat. Their batting lineup, featuring the likes of Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran, has the potential to be explosive, but they will need to build partnerships and anchor the innings more effectively. Gurbaz, who started brightly in the last match, will be a key player to watch. Afghanistan's strength lies in its world-class spin attack. Led by captain Rashid Khan, the team boasts a formidable trio of spinners including Mujeeb Ur Rahman and Noor Ahmad. Mujeeb's economical spell in the last match showcased his ability to trouble batters with his variations. With the Sharjah pitch historically favoring spinners, this attack could be the difference-maker for Afghanistan. The pace attack, featuring Fazalhaq Farooqi and Fareed Ahmad Malik, will also be vital in providing early breakthroughs and containing the opposition. The hosts, UAE, are also coming off a loss to Pakistan in their first match. They put up a valiant fight while chasing a large total but ultimately fell short. This loss, however, will not deter them, as they will be playing in front of their home crowd and will be motivated to bounce back. Captain Muhammad Waseem leads a squad that blends experience with promising young talent. The likes of Alishan Sharafu and Asif Khan will be crucial in the batting department, while the bowling will be spearheaded by Junaid Siddique and Muhammad Jawadullah. While both teams are looking for their first win in the series, Afghanistan, with its strong spin department and T20I experience, will be considered the favorites. Their bowling attack is particularly well-suited for the conditions at Sharjah. However, the UAE, playing at home, will be determined to cause an upset.
